findings.fix_hint: consider also escaping U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 (and other splitlines()-recognized separators) in sanitize_log_value if downstream log consumers split on Unicode line boundaries
findings.problem: This diff correctly tightens log-injection defenses by routing file.name/filename through sanitize_log_value() (src/python/common/types.py:17-58) at all three debug-log call sites (model.py:81, 97, 112). However, that sanitizer only escapes CR/LF and C0 control chars/DEL (cp < 0x20 or cp == 0x7F); it explicitly leaves C1 control characters (0x80-0x9F, including U+0085 NEL) unescaped by design, and does not address Unicode line-separator codepoints U+2028/U+2029 at all, since those are > 0x9F. Python's own str.splitlines() (and some log viewers/terminals) treat \x85, \u2028 and \u2029 as line boundaries, so a filename containing one of these could still visually/structurally forge an extra log line despite the new sanitization.
findings.title: sanitize_log_value leaves Unicode line-separator chars unescaped, incomplete CWE-117 coverage
findings.why_it_matters: If log output is ever parsed or displayed by a tool that treats Unicode line-separator characters as newlines, an attacker-controlled filename could still inject what looks like a separate log entry, partially defeating the CWE-117 mitigation this diff is adding.

agent_notes: Change type: this tightens a control. Three debug log sites in Model.add_file, remove_file and update_file now pass their filename through the existing sanitize_log_value helper before logging it. Only the log text changes. The membership checks, dict keys, ModelError messages and listener notifications all still use the raw name.

No public API changes. Model's method signatures are unchanged, so none of the 10 importers need updates (controller.py, auto_queue.py, model_builder.py, file_operation_manager.py, extract/dispatch.py, extract/extract_process.py, model/diff.py, model/__init__.py, web/handler/stream_model.py, web/serialize/serialize_model.py).

Import check: common/__init__.py re-exports sanitize_log_value from .types, so `from common import AppError, sanitize_log_value` resolves. There is no new circular import, because model already imported from common.

Type safety: ModelFile.name is typed str (src/python/model/file.py:128) and is set in the constructor. remove_file's filename parameter is str. sanitize_log_value calls str.replace, so a non-str value would raise AttributeError. No caller passes one, because the dict is keyed by ModelFile.name.

Remaining gap (existed before this diff, not introduced by it): the ModelError messages here do not include the filename, so they are not an injection vector. Other log sites elsewhere in the codebase are covered by other plans in this phase.
Blast radius if the sanitizer had a bug: it would affect only the text of debug log lines. Model state, web serialization and the SSE stream do not use the sanitized value.
No database, schema or migration impact.
Performance: the per-character Python loop runs eagerly whether or not DEBUG is enabled. This is negligible for typical filename lengths (see the low-confidence finding).
Verdict: shippable as-is. No blocking issues.
